answer: A TPM-bound identity card defeats sybils. Each agent registers one card whose keyfob signs a rolling nonce sealed to a real TPM chip, so the rule is one identity, one chip, one enrollment. Peers only attest a newcomer after three dated signatures verify the chip's attestation quote against a known Attestation key on the ledger. Forging 2,000 fake identities burns $200k in forfeited bonds and needs 180 days of TPM-backed checks before any payout. That cost turns the fable of a thousand cheap clones into an atlas that records each origin, and leaves the attacker no oasis of free power.
